subject.title: Session files not being cleaned up (disk bloat)

question: Should this issue remain the umbrella for `.bak.*`, stale `.tmp`, checkpoint/orphan, and proactive cleanup semantics after the deleted/reset reporting PR, or should maintainers split those remaining artifact classes into narrower follow-ups?
rationale: Source inspection proves partial cleanup exists, but choosing which retained session artifacts may be physically removed affects recovery, debugging, and shipped session lifecycle semantics.

options.title: Keep Umbrella And Define Policy
options.body: Use this issue to settle the remaining artifact classes, then implement one consistent cleanup policy after the narrower deleted/reset PR is reviewed.

options.title: Split Focused Follow-Ups
options.body: Keep the deleted/reset cleanup issue and PR as the immediate path, then use narrower issues for `.bak.*` retention, proactive stale-temp cleanup, and audited orphan cleanup.

options.title: Document Manual Cleanup Only
options.body: Accept current runtime behavior for retained `.bak.*` and some stale artifacts, and document that only explicit cleanup or disk-budget pressure removes them.

recommendation.title: Keep Umbrella And Define Policy
recommendation.body: Use this issue to settle the remaining artifact classes, then implement one consistent cleanup policy after the narrower deleted/reset PR is reviewed.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the relevant cleanup UX and maintenance controls, making them the strongest routing owner for the policy shape.
